context:
Final verification for the remediation program. The tag and the pypi approval stay owner-only. DECISION GATE: if any acceptance line fails, file the gap as a new item with the run evidence and ask the owner whether to release anyway; do not tune gates outside the rubric to make it pass.

Owner decision 2026-11-11: removed the dependency on dropped rv2r-08 and its acceptance line (no infrastructure merges during the release window, G13 hold history), because the owner retired the G13 freeze on 2026-11-06. This next release is now also the base for the rv2r-14 maintenance-line rehearsal. An adversarial audit on 2026-11-11 (develop fc91789f, PR #4086 ec942c73) found the v0.5.0-based rehearsal likely to fail: develop's UAT harness passes parallel_pipeline_task_num=1 to Doris, which v0.5.0 rejects as an unknown platform option, and develop's 4 GiB Doris/SingleStore limits need product fixes (#4069, #4071) absent from v0.5.0. It would also need a multi-thousand-line backport that is deleted afterwards.

Owner decisions 2026-11-11: the next release is 0.5.1 from develop. The agent prepares and merges the release-prep PR now (version and changelog) and gets develop releasable, but pushes no tag, rc or final, until BenchBox #4062 lands with Theseus v0.2.9 (the owner chose to wait for the Theseus session rather than decouple or take over). Then v0.5.1rc1 to TestPyPI, then v0.5.1 final with the owner's pypi approval; the agent pushes tags. The rv2r-14 rehearsal then cuts release/0.5.x from the v0.5.1 tag (which carries maintenance-line support).

2026-11-11: 0.5.1 release-prep PR #4097 (head d6817eae, no tag) is blocked on core's windows-tests leg: a release-identity change selects the whole fast suite (~33k tests) run serially against a 30-minute timeout (v0.5.0's #3940 took 27 min); three attempts gave a timeout, a Python fatal error, and one Windows-only failure (test_show_cli_reconstructs_legacy_command, Rich truncation). Owner decision: fix the truncation and run the Windows leg with pytest-xdist, keeping selection and timeouts; then rebase #4097, rerun release-check and land it. Theseus v0.2.9 was released 2026-11-11 12:51 UTC and #4062 is active again (head 2961f4e2).
